title: Policy for Trading in Company Securities

tiers.name: Everyone
tiers.description: Designated Persons and all other employees and strategic contractors of the Company or its subsidiaries, and their family and associates. Only the Insider Trading Prohibition and Confidential Information obligations apply to this tier; the substantive Prohibited Periods and Other Restrictions in the Policy do not.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All directors and officers, KMP, the Israel office manager, all IT staff, strategic contractors who have specifically agreed to be subject to the restrictions, and any other person designated by the Board. Subject to the whole Trading Policy (Prohibited Periods, Other Restrictions in section 6, clearance procedure).

tiers.name: Directors and KMP
tiers.description: Subset of Designated Persons who are directors or key management personnel; must obtain prior written approval from the Board of Directors before any trade, even outside a Prohibited Period.

tiers.name: Other Designated Persons
tiers.description: Designated Persons who are not directors or KMP; do not need approval to trade outside Prohibited Periods, but need prior written clearance from the CEO (or CFO/Company Secretary) to trade during a Prohibited Period.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18, an unlisted body corporate controlled by the Designated Person, a trust of which the Designated Person is trustee and beneficiary (or of which those persons are beneficiaries), or any other person over whom the Designated Person has significant influence or control. Designated Persons must take reasonable steps, including notice of Blackout Periods, to prevent Connected Persons from trading in a way prohibited under the Policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: has not vested in the member; or has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock

windows.end_anchor: one business day after release of the Company's Annual Financial Report
one business day after release of the Consolidated Interim Financial Report
one business day after release of the Company's Q3 quarterly report
one business day after release of the Company's Q1 quarterly report

windows.start_anchor: 2 weeks before the holding of any general meeting of shareholders
windows.end_anchor: next business day after the holding of the general meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose an Additional Prohibited Period from time to time while considering matters that would require disclosure but for the Listing Rule 3.1A carve-out. Confidential: an Appendix 3Y need only disclose trading during a Blackout Period, not an Additional Prohibited Period, 'so that an entity does not have to disclose to the market that it has imposed such a prohibition, which would signal the fact that it is considering a potentially market sensitive matter.'

rules.detail: Dealing in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities (which has no venue limit) is banned except for dealing permitted under this Policy; for directors and KMP that means prior written Board approval is required before any trade, including a derivative, at all times, even outside a Prohibited Period.
rules.evidence: Any director or KMP must not trade in the Company Securities ... unless the director or KMP obtains prior written approval by the Board of Directors of the Company. This is the case even if the proposed transaction is outside of a Prohibited Period.

rules.detail: Same dealing-in-financial-products restriction applies, but clearance from the CEO (or CFO/Company Secretary) is only required for trading during a Prohibited Period; outside a Prohibited Period no clearance is needed.
rules.evidence: A Designated Person who is not a director or KMP does not need approval to trade in Company Securities outside of Prohibited Periods.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no exception, on entering transactions or arrangements with anyone that limit exposure to risk relating to remuneration that has not vested.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: has not vested in the member;

rules.detail: The same absolute ban extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: or has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock;

rules.detail: Once vested and no longer subject to a holding lock, the absolute hedging ban in (i) no longer applies; dealing in financial products over Company Securities is still restricted to types of dealing permitted by law or under this Policy, i.e. it must be cleared under section 7.
rules.evidence: deal in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.

rules.detail: The hedging restriction in section 6 applies only to Designated Persons; employees who are not Designated Persons are subject only to the Insider Trading Prohibition and Confidential Information obligations.

Monetisation is not named. Company Securities includes 'any hedging arrangement, financial instrument or derivative of Weebit ordinary shares' with no venue limit, and Dealing includes entering into an agreement to acquire or dispose; a monetisation structure such as a prepaid forward is therefore caught as dealing in a financial product requiring clearance under section 7, or is an outright breach of 6(d)(ii) if not a permitted type of dealing.
rules.evidence: any hedging arrangement, financial instrument or derivative of Weebit ordinary shares

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling, defined as selling financial products the Designated Person does not own with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short selling (being the selling by a Designated Person of financial products they do not own with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price) of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not listed within the scope of Company Securities or the concept of dealing.

CFDs are not named. They fall within 'derivative or other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities' referenced in the short-term/speculative trading ban and within the section 6(d)(ii) dealing-in-financial-products restriction, so a CFD would need to avoid the short-term/speculative characterisation and be cleared as a permitted dealing.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Company Securities or in derivative or other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Outright ban on margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities; no clearance route or exemption authority is provided for this restriction.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending ban applies only to Designated Persons; employees who are not Designated Persons are not restricted by this Policy from margin lending.

Granting security over Company Securities to support any financing is caught by the blanket ban on 'other secured financing arrangements'; the only carve-out is a secured lender's enforcement sale under section 8(f), and that carve-out does not extend to an arrangement that was itself prohibited under 6(a).
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on margin lending or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Company Securities, for all Designated Persons and their closely related parties; the stated grounds are that loan terms may force a sale during a Prohibited Period or while holding Inside Information. Designated Persons must consult the CEO if uncertain whether an arrangement is prohibited.
rules.evidence: The grounds for this include that the terms may require Company Securities to be sold during a Prohibited Period or when the Designated Person possesses Inside Information.

rules.detail: The secured financing ban applies only to Designated Persons; employees who are not Designated Persons are not restricted by this Policy from secured financing.

No short term or speculative trading in Company Securities or in derivatives/financial products over them; short term means less than a 6 month period. Carve-out for selling shares shortly after exercising options or rights.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Company Securities or in derivative or other financial products issued over or in respect of Company Securities. Short term means in less than a 6 month period.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: 1 business day after the dealing has occurred
clearance.evidence: Any director or KMP must not trade in the Company Securities, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to above unless the director or KMP obtains prior written approval by the Board of Directors of the Company. This is the case even if the proposed transaction is outside of a Prohibited Period.

clearance.approver: Chief Executive Officer, or in his absence the Chief Financial Officer or Company Secretary (Approving Officer)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 1 business day after the dealing has occurred
clearance.evidence: A Designated Person, other than a director or KMP, must not trade in the Company Securities during a Prohibited Period, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to above, unless the other Designated Person obtains prior written clearance from the Chief Executive Officer or in his absence, the Chief Financial Officer or Company Secretary.

carve_outs: selling shares shortly after exercising options or rights issued to the Designated Person by the Company
short_term.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in Company Securities ... Short term means in less than a 6 month period. This does not apply to selling shares shortly after exercising options or rights issued to the Designated Person by the Company.

exceptions.approver: Board of Directors (directors/KMP) or Approving Officer (other Designated Persons)
exceptions.evidence: if the person granting the prior written clearance ... is satisfied that the person seeking the clearance does not possess unpublished price sensitive information about the Company and the person seeking clearance is in severe financial hardship;

exceptions.approver: Board of Directors (directors/KMP) or Approving Officer (other Designated Persons)
exceptions.evidence: there are other circumstances deemed to be exceptional by the person granting the prior written clearance;

exceptions.approver: Board of Directors (directors/KMP) or Approving Officer (other Designated Persons)
exceptions.evidence: where trading is required for compliance with a court order or court enforceable undertakings or for some other legal or regulatory requirement.
transfers of securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person is a beneficiary;

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

where the Designated Person is a trustee, trading in the Company Securities by that trust provided the Designated Persons is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Designated Person;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer;

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement if the agreement is prohibited by this policy.

the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right ... falls during a Prohibited Period and the Company has been in an exceptionally long Prohibited Period.

exemption_authority: The Board of Directors (for directors/KMP) or Approving Officer (CEO, or CFO/Company Secretary, for other Designated Persons) may permit trading in a Prohibited Period only for severe financial hardship, other circumstances they deem exceptional (both conditional on not possessing unpublished price sensitive information), or a court order/legal requirement (s5.4). Clearance may be granted or refused in Weebit's discretion without giving reasons, and refusal must be kept confidential by the person who sought it (s7.4).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for all Designated Persons, with no clearance or exemption route, so the secured-financing component of the structure cannot lawfully be implemented.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights ... does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement if the agreement is prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The exclusion for a secured lender's enforcement sale gives no comfort here because the underlying loan arrangement (any secured financing over Company Securities) is itself banned outright under 6(a).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any director or KMP must not trade in the Company Securities ... unless the director or KMP obtains prior written approval by the Board of Directors ... This is the case even if the proposed transaction is outside of a Prohibited Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even outside any blackout, a director or KMP needs Board approval, granted or refused at the Board's unfettered discretion, before entering the derivative legs of a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a written clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A refusal of clearance to enter, unwind or roll a collar cannot be disclosed by the executive, complicating coordination with the bank on timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: will be valid for the period of not longer than 10 business days from the time which it is given ... Should the intended dealing in Weebit's securities not take effect within the clearance period then the permission to trade must be refreshed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution of the derivative legs (and any later unwind or roll) must occur within the default 10 business day clearance window or fresh clearance must be sought, adding execution-timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a Designated Person must confirm in writing to the relevant Approving Officer or the Board of Directors in the case of a director or KMP, within 1 business day from when the dealing in Company Securities has occurred, the number of Company Securities affected and the relevant parties to the dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank counterparty's identity and the trade's terms would need to be reported internally within 1 business day of dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons should consult with the Chief Executive Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement is prohibited under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is an informal escalation path to test whether a bespoke collar structure would be treated as prohibited secured financing before entering it.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under Weebit's policy, though an unfunded overlay could in principle be cleared. Directors and KMP may deal in Company Securities, including entering OTC derivatives, only with prior written Board approval at all times (even outside Prohibited Periods); other Designated Persons need equivalent clearance from the CEO/CFO/Company Secretary only during a Prohibited Period. Section 6(a), however, unconditionally bans margin lending and any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Company Securities for all Designated Persons, with no clearance or exemption route, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares cannot be implemented. Hedging is also absolutely prohibited while the shares are unvested or vested but subject to a holding lock, and any lender enforcement-sale carve-out does not rescue an arrangement that was itself prohibited. Any clearance obtained is valid for only 10 business days and must be refreshed if unused, so only the put/call overlay, unsecured and cleared, could be executed, and only outside Blackout and Additional Prohibited Periods.
